seo_title: Microsoft Excel & Business Reporting Course | Nova Skills
seo_description: Learn Excel formulas, XLOOKUP, PivotTables, charts and reporting in 6 weeks (48h). Build 3 practical Excel projects. Fee ₹6,900.

overview.heading: What You Will Learn
overview.description: Learn Microsoft Excel through real business tasks, formulas, data cleaning, PivotTables, charts and practical reporting. Build professional spreadsheets for sales, attendance, inventory and expense analysis while developing accuracy, troubleshooting and responsible AI-assisted working habits.
overview.expanded_copy_1: Learn to organize business data, create dependable formulas, validate entries and generate useful reports in Microsoft Excel. Practise common office tasks including sales tracking, attendance monitoring, inventory analysis and expense summaries.
overview.expanded_copy_2: Build confidence with modern Excel functions, PivotTables, charts and basic data-import workflows. Complete a practical reporting portfolio with documented checks that demonstrate your ability to calculate, analyze and explain business information accurately.
overview.main_value_proposition: Business-Ready Excel Skills Built Around Accuracy and Practical Reporting.
overview.learning_journey: Prepare Data → Calculate → Validate → Analyze → Visualize → Reconcile → Report → Explain

prerequisites: Basic computer skills (file management, typing, mouse navigation)
Basic arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, percentages)
No prior Microsoft Excel experience or programming required
target_audience: College students preparing for workplace office roles
Job seekers targeting administrative, operational, or coordinator positions
Office executives and administrative staff looking to upgrade spreadsheet reporting
Sales coordinators and account executives tracking sales data
HR assistants and payroll coordinators monitoring attendance records
Inventory coordinators and retail management staff managing stock registers
Small business owners seeking reliable monthly reporting without costly software
Early-career operations staff building foundational business data skills
learning_outcomes: Use relative, absolute and mixed references.
Explain INDEX/MATCH at an awareness level.
Compare source totals with report totals.
Create an attendance or expense report.
Recognize the limitations of the analysis.
hands_on_tech: Microsoft Excel for Microsoft 365 (Windows Desktop preferred)
Microsoft Copilot in Excel (Optional, where licensed)
CSV Business Practice Datasets (Sales, HR Attendance, Operational Expenses, Inventory)

modules.title: Excel Foundations & Data Quality
modules.objective: Develop correct foundational habits for working with business spreadsheets and structured data.
lessons: 1.1 Introduction to Microsoft Excel: Spreadsheet purpose.; Office workflows.; Business reporting.; Common practical applications.
1.2 Excel Interface: Ribbon.; Formula bar.; Name box.; Worksheets.; Workbook navigation.; Quick Access Toolbar awareness.
1.3 Workbook Fundamentals: Create.; Open.; Save.; Save As.; File formats.; Worksheet naming.
1.4 Cells and Ranges: Row.; Column.; Cell address.; Range.; Selection.
1.5 Data Entry: Text.; Numeric data.; Dates.; Percentages.; Currency.; Blank cells.
1.6 Data Types: Number vs text.; Dates as serial values.; Text-based IDs.; Common errors.
1.7 Cell References: Relative references.; Absolute references.; Mixed references.; Fill behaviour.
1.8 Basic Calculation: Arithmetic operators.; Order of operations.; Basic formula syntax.
1.9 Essential Formatting: Number formats.; Currency.; Percentages.; Dates.; Decimal precision.
1.10 Professional Formatting: Alignment.; Readable headings.; Consistent fonts.; Borders.; Table formatting.; Controlled colours.
1.11 Excel Tables: Insert Table.; Headers.; Table names.; Auto-expanding table rows.; Calculated columns.
1.12 Structured Business Data: One record per row.; One variable per column.; Unique column headings.; No merged cells in source tables.; No blank separator rows.
1.13 Sorting: Single-column sorting.; Multi-column sorting.; Avoiding partial-range sorting errors.
1.14 Filtering: AutoFilter.; Date filters.; Numeric filters.; Text filters.; Clear filters.
1.15 Data Quality: Missing values.; Duplicate records.; Wrong data types.; Inconsistent spelling.; Invalid dates.
1.16 Error Prevention: Correct headings.; Unique identifiers.; Consistent data entry.; Input documentation.; Source preservation.
1.17 Freeze Panes: Maintaining header visibility.; Navigation.
1.18 Basic Worksheet Protection Awareness: Preventing accidental formula changes.; Protection is not a substitute for information security.
1.19 File Organization: Version naming.; Source files.; Reporting files.; Backups.
1.20 Basic Troubleshooting: #### display.; Number stored as text.; Incorrect dates.; Broken references.; Formula entered as text.

modules.title: Business Formulas & Functions
modules.objective: Apply essential Excel formulas to realistic business reporting problems and independently verify the results.
lessons: 2.1 Formula Fundamentals: Equals sign.; Operators.; Arguments.; Function structure.; Parentheses.
2.2 References in Formulas: Relative.; Absolute.; Mixed.; Copying formulas.
2.3 Basic Functions: SUM.; AVERAGE.; MIN.; MAX.; COUNT.; COUNTA.; Teach as building blocks, not the entire assessment focus.
2.4 SUMIF vs SUMIFS: Conditional sums.; Multiple criteria.; Dates.; Product categories.; Salespersons.
2.5 COUNTIF vs COUNTIFS: Counting records.; Attendance.; Status reports.; Multiple conditions.
2.6 IF: Logical tests.; Business rules.; Status labels.; Eligibility conditions.
2.7 IFS: Multiple conditions.; Ordered tests.; Default cases.; Appropriate use.
2.8 AND / OR: Combined conditions.; Validity checks.; Eligibility rules.
2.9 IFERROR: Handling expected error cases.; Clear messages.; Formula quality.; Important: Do not teach IFERROR as a method of hiding all errors without investigation.
2.10 Lookup Concepts: Unique identifiers.; Lookup tables.; Exact matches.; Missing values.
2.11 XLOOKUP: Lookup value.; Lookup array.; Return array.; Exact match.; Not-found handling.
2.12 XLOOKUP Business Examples: Product price lookup.; Employee department lookup.; Inventory category lookup.; Commission category lookup.
2.13 Duplicate Lookup Keys: First-match behaviour.; Data reliability.; Why identifiers matter.

2.14 INDEX/MATCH Awareness: Concept.; Why older workbooks use it.; Compatibility.; Simple alternative lookup explanation.; Avoid making complex INDEX/MATCH combinations a major advanced specialization.
2.15 VLOOKUP Compatibility Awareness: Recognize existing VLOOKUP formulas.; Understand approximate vs exact match.; Common legacy workbook considerations.
2.16 Text Functions: LEFT.; RIGHT.; MID.; LEN.; TRIM.; CONCAT or TEXTJOIN where supported.; UPPER/LOWER/PROPER.
2.17 Text Cleanup: Extra spaces.; Standardizing codes.; Extracting fields.; Joining text.
2.18 Date Functions: TODAY.; YEAR.; MONTH.; DAY.; EOMONTH awareness.; Date differences.
2.19 Business Date Calculations: Report month.; Attendance month.; Due-date status.; Ageing awareness without advanced finance modeling.
2.20 Common Formula Errors: #N/A.; #VALUE!.; #REF!.; #DIV/0!.; #NAME?.; #SPILL! awareness.
2.21 Formula Auditing: Evaluate Formula.; Trace precedents/dependents.; Formula bar review.; Test cases.
2.22 Formula Verification: Manual calculations.; Small known datasets.; Expected-result examples.; Independent totals.
2.23 Structured References: Table column references.; Automatically filling formulas.; Expanding source tables.
2.24 Business Formula Documentation: Meaning of calculated fields.; Assumptions.; Calculation logic.

modules.title: Modern Excel & Data Management
modules.objective: Use modern spreadsheet management tools to organize, validate, clean and retrieve business information.
lessons: 3.1 Data Management Principles: Source data.; Calculated data.; Reports.; Data integrity.; Consistency.
3.2 Excel Tables: Structured references.; Calculated columns.; Table expansion.; Table naming.
3.3 Conditional Formatting: Highlight cell rules.; Greater/less than.; Duplicate values.; Colour scales.; Data bars.; Formula-based rules at a suitable introductory level.
3.4 Practical Conditional Formatting: Overdue tasks.; Low inventory.; High expenses.; Attendance exceptions.; Outlier awareness.
3.5 Data Validation: Lists.; Whole numbers.; Decimal ranges.; Dates.; Input messages.; Error alerts.
3.6 Drop-Down Lists: Allowed categories.; Department names.; Employee status.; Expense types.
3.7 Validation Limitations: Pasted data may bypass some controls.; Users can change validation.; Data checks remain necessary.
3.8 Duplicate Handling: Identify duplicates.; Unique record keys.; Conditional formatting.; Remove Duplicates.; Preserve original data.
3.9 Missing Values: Blank fields.; Null concept.; Required input checks.; Appropriate correction.
3.10 Inconsistent Data: Product names.; Department names.; Leading/trailing spaces.; Date formatting.; Data-type mismatches.
3.11 Find and Replace: Appropriate use.; Scope awareness.; Avoid accidental global changes.
3.12 Text to Columns: Delimited text.; Basic import cleanup.; Avoiding unintended overwrites.
3.13 Introduction to Dynamic Arrays: Spill behaviour.; Multi-cell results.; Dynamic resizing.; Version requirements.
3.14 FILTER: Extract records meeting conditions.; Handle empty-result cases.; Use safe sample data.
3.15 UNIQUE: Distinct products.; Unique departments.; Category lists.; Duplicate investigation.
3.16 SORT: Sorting a dynamic array.; Ascending/descending.; Suitable business examples.
3.17 Combining Dynamic Functions: FILTER and SORT.; UNIQUE and SORT.; Appropriate intermediate complexity.
3.18 Spill Ranges: Understanding spill outputs.; Blocking cells.; #SPILL! errors.; Dynamic range references.

3.19 Excel Table Compatibility: Structured source data.; Dynamic-array formulas placed in the worksheet grid outside the Excel Table.; Important: Spilled-array formulas are not supported inside Excel Tables themselves.
3.20 Dynamic Array Version Awareness: Excel for Microsoft 365.; Supported newer perpetual editions.; Older Excel limitations.
3.21 Simple Inventory Data: Item code.; Category.; Current quantity.; Reorder point.; Status.; Supplier field.
3.22 Attendance Data: Employee/student ID.; Date.; Status.; Department/class.; Reporting period.
3.23 Expense Data: Date.; Category.; Description.; Payment mode.; Amount.; Approval status.
3.24 Data Quality Checklist: Correct types.; Complete records.; Unique IDs.; No unintended duplicates.; Appropriate validation.

faq.question: What is Microsoft Excel — Business Reporting & Data Analysis?
faq.answer: It is a practical Excel certification covering formulas, structured data, data validation, PivotTables, charts and business reporting.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Six weeks, with 48 learning hours.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: ₹6,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified fee and tax policy.

faq.question: Is the course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It begins with Excel fundamentals.

faq.question: Do I need prior Excel knowledge?
faq.answer: No. Basic computer and arithmetic skills are sufficient.

faq.question: Which Excel version is used?
faq.answer: Microsoft Excel for Microsoft 365, preferably the Windows desktop version.

faq.question: Will I learn Excel formulas?
faq.answer: Yes, including SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, IF, IFS, IFERROR and XLOOKUP.

faq.question: Will I learn XLOOKUP?
faq.answer: Yes. XLOOKUP is part of the mandatory curriculum.

faq.question: Will I learn VLOOKUP and INDEX/MATCH?
faq.answer: Students receive useful awareness of legacy lookup methods, while XLOOKUP is the main modern lookup function.

faq.question: What are dynamic arrays?
faq.answer: They are modern Excel formulas capable of returning results across multiple worksheet cells.

faq.question: Will I learn FILTER, UNIQUE and SORT?
faq.answer: Yes. These are included in the modern Excel module.

faq.question: Why do some formulas not work in older Excel versions?
faq.answer: Modern functions depend on the Excel version. Older installations may lack XLOOKUP or dynamic-array functionality.

faq.question: Will I learn data validation?
faq.answer: Yes, including suitable restrictions and drop-down lists.

faq.question: Will I learn conditional formatting?
faq.answer: Yes, for useful tasks such as highlighting exceptions and business statuses.

faq.question: Will I learn PivotTables?
faq.answer: Yes. PivotTables are a major part of the course.

faq.question: Will I learn charts and reporting?
faq.answer: Yes. Students practise charts, PivotCharts, KPIs and business summaries.

faq.question: Will I learn dashboards?
faq.answer: The course teaches practical reporting summaries with charts and PivotTables, not complex enterprise BI dashboards.

faq.question: Will I learn Power Query?
faq.answer: Yes, at an introductory level for importing and preparing data.

faq.question: Will I learn Power BI?
faq.answer: No. Power BI belongs to an advanced MIS/Business Intelligence pathway.

faq.question: Will I learn VBA or macros?
faq.answer: No. VBA automation is outside this certification.

faq.question: Will I learn Python in Excel?
faq.answer: No. The course concentrates on Excel foundations and applied reporting.

faq.question: Is Copilot required?
faq.answer: No. Copilot is optional and depends on licensing and feature availability.

faq.question: Can AI help with Excel formulas?
faq.answer: Yes, but students must understand and independently verify all formula outputs.

faq.question: What business reports will I create?
faq.answer: A sales tracker, an expense or attendance report and a final Excel reporting workbook.

faq.question: What will my final capstone include?
faq.answer: Structured data, validation, formulas, a PivotTable, charts, quality checks and a management summary.

faq.question: Will I learn CSV import?
faq.answer: Yes, including data types, encoding, dates and common import issues.

faq.question: Will I learn to identify spreadsheet errors?
faq.answer: Yes. Formula errors, invalid data and report reconciliation are important parts of the course.

faq.question: Is this suitable for office executives?
faq.answer: Yes. The content focuses on common office reporting and data analysis work.

faq.question: Can small business owners take this course?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers practical sales, expense and inventory reporting applications.

faq.question: What can I study next?
faq.answer: Suitable progression may include advanced Excel, Business Productivity Mastery and longer MIS/Business Intelligence programs. ---
